newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dataquest sees Japan 1997 PC shipments up 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dataquest sees Japan 1997 PC shipments up 27 pct.

text.p: Japanese personal computer (PC) shipments in 1997 should grow 27.0 percent year-on-year to 9.61 million units, after rising an actual 32.7 percent last year, market research firm Dataquest said.
Dataquest attributed the growth in the Japanese market to the low penetration of PCs in Japanese companies and homes and the growing use and enhancement of the Internet in Japan.
Though the growth rate here is slowing, the Japanese market is still showing strong growth compared with other markets in the world, Dataquest said in a statement.
The increase was smaller than a year-on-year 70.5 percent rise in 1995 but exceeded the average growth rate on the global market of 17.8 percent in 1996, it said.
In actual number of PCs, shipments on the Japanese market totalled 7.57 million units in 1996, while 9.61 million units are forecasted to be shipped this year, it said.
Dataquest forecast early last year that 1996 shipments in Japan would be 8.01 million units.
In the United States, PC shipments in 1996 grew 13.6 percent from the previous year, it said.
NEC Corp was the top PC vendor in Japan in 1996, capturing a 32.0 percent of the market share, followed by Fujitsu Ltd and IBM Japan Ltd, a unit of International Business Machines Corp, it said.
Apple Computers Inc, which held third position in 1995, fell to fourth place in 1996.
Toshiba Corp stayed in fifth place, but nearly doubled its market share, going from 3.8 percent in 1995 to 6.4 percent last year.
